items.title: The normalized type-A Hecke algebra and its bar involution
items.statement: Let n≥1 and A=Z[v±1]. For n≥2, H_v(n) is the type-A algebra with quadratic relation H_s²=1+(v⁻¹−v)H_s and the braid and distant-commutation relations; H_v(1)=A. With q=v⁻² and H_w=v^{ℓ(w)}T_w, the generic standard basis specializes and rescales to an A-basis, with H_wH_s=H_{ws} on length ascent and H_{ws}+(v⁻¹−v)H_w on descent. The bar assignment is semilinear, v↦v⁻¹ and H_s↦H_s⁻¹=H_s−(v⁻¹−v); its well-defined involution and value ι(H_w)=H_{w⁻¹}⁻¹ are supplied by lem-the-hecke-bar-involution-is-well-defined.
items.strategy: A definition item. (i) The coefficient base change q↦v⁻² and rescaling H_{s_i}=vT_i identify the two presentations; the reverse assignment is T_i=v⁻¹H_{s_i}. The standard-basis theorem gives the basis, and rescaling gives the displayed multiplication rule. (ii) The quadratic relation gives H_{s_i}^{-1}=H_{s_i}−(v⁻¹−v). (iii) The semilinear bar assignment is declared here; its descent and involutivity are proved by the assigned lemma. No Choice is used.

items.title: The Hecke bar involution is well defined
items.statement: In H_v(n) there is a unique A-semilinear unital ring involution ι with ι(v)=v⁻¹ and ι(H_{s_i})=H_{s_i}⁻¹. It is multiplicative and satisfies ι²=id and ι(H_w)=H_{w⁻¹}⁻¹ for every w∈S_n; consequently each H_w is invertible and ι(H_{w⁻¹})=H_w⁻¹.
items.strategy: Direct verification on the presentation. Extend the normalized definition's candidate free-algebra substitution H_s ↦ H_s−(v⁻¹−v). The quadratic relation makes its quotient image H_s⁻¹ and gives the semilinearly conjugate quadratic relation. The braid relator is a palindrome, so its inverse is the braid relator for the inverse generators; distant inverse generators commute. The assignment therefore descends, is unique on generators, and squares to the identity. Reverse a reduced word to obtain the formula on H_w. No Choice is used.

items.title: Basic properties of the Bruhat order on $S_n$
items.statement: Let ≤ be the rank-inequality order on the zero-based S_n of def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group, and identify it with the one-based realization by shifting inputs and values by 1. (a) This order is the strong Bruhat order of type A: the transitive closure of covers x→tx where t is a transposition and ℓ(tx)=ℓ(x)+1. (b) If y≤w then ℓ(y)≤ℓ(w), with equality iff y=w; every saturated chain has ℓ(w)−ℓ(y) steps; and y≤w iff y⁻¹≤w⁻¹. (c) y≤w iff for every reduced expression w=s_{i1}⋯s_{ik}, y is a reduced subword. (d) For every simple reflection s, if y≤w and ℓ(sy)>ℓ(y), then y≤sw; if y≤w and ℓ(sw)<ℓ(w), then sy≤w. (e) Every interval [y,w] is finite and [y,w]={y}∪⋃_{y→a≤w}[a,w].
items.strategy: Direct. Identify the zero- and one-based S_n models and construct its standard type-A root realization. Show strong covers decrease the rank matrix, then prove the converse by induction using rank-matrix lifting for a simple left descent. The finite-Weyl supplier gives the reduced-subword characterization. Derive both lifting implications from a reduced word beginning with a left descent, and decompose each finite interval by its first cover. Correct the scaffold equality clause to include y=w=id.

items.title: Reversal anti-involution commutes with the Hecke bar
items.statement: The presented normalized Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ has an involutive $A$-linear anti-automorphism $\flat$ defined by $\flat(H_{s_i})=H_{s_i}$. It satisfies $\flat(H_w)=H_{w^{-1}}$ for every $w\in S_n$ and commutes with the bar involution: $\flat\circ\iota=\iota\circ\flat$.
items.strategy: Extend reversal of words from the free algebra; check the quadratic, braid, and commutation relators; then verify the two compositions agree on coefficients and generators.

items.title: The $R$-coefficient recursion, support, degree bounds and inversion
items.statement: For $n\ge1$, let $r_{y,w}\in A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the $R$-coefficients of [[def-bruhat-interval-and-r-polynomials]]. (a) **Recursion.** Let $w\in S_n$ and let $s=s_i$ be a simple reflection with $sw<w$. Then for every $y\in S_n$ $$r_{y,w}=r_{sy,sw}\quad\text{if }sy<y,\qquad r_{y,w}=r_{sy,sw}+(v-v^{-1})\,r_{y,sw}\quad\text{if }sy>y .$$ (b) **Support.** $r_{y,w}\ne0$ implies $y\le w$, and $r_{w,w}=1$. (c) **Degree and parity.** For $y\le w$, with $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$: $r_{y,w}\in v^{-d}\,\mathbb Z[v^{2},v^{-2}]$; the term of least $v$-degree is $\mathrm{sgn}(y)\,\mathrm{sgn}(w)\,v^{-d}$, and the term of largest $v$-degree is $v^{d}$. (d) **Symmetry.** $\overline{r_{y,w}}=\mathrm{sgn}(y)\mathrm{sgn}(w)r_{y,w}$ and $r_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=r_{y,w}$. (e) **Matrix inversion.** $\sum_{y\in S_n} r_{x,y}\,\overline{r_{y,z}}=\delta_{x,z}$ for all $x,z$; equivalently the triangular matrices $R=(r_{x,y})$, $\bar R$ satisfy $R\bar R=\bar RR=1$. Here $\mathrm{sgn}(y)=(-1)^{\ell(y)}$ and all coefficients are kept in the variable $v$ of this page.
items.strategy: (a) Derive the left generator multiplication rule from the presentation, expand $\iota(H_sH_{sw})$ and compare standard-basis coefficients; use the resulting recursion for (b)–(d). (b) Induct on $\ell(w)$ and use the reduced-subword characterization for each recursion branch. (c) Track parity and both extreme terms in the same induction. (d) Induct on the recursion for bar symmetry and apply [[lem-reversal-anti-involution-commutes-with-hecke-bar]] for inverse-index symmetry. (e) Apply $\iota^2=1$ to the coefficient expansion and then apply coefficient bar for the other matrix identity. All inductions are finite; no Choice is used.

items.title: Verma's sign identity over Bruhat intervals
items.statement: For all $x<z$ in $S_n$, with $\mathrm{sgn}(y)=(-1)^{\ell(y)}$, $$\sum_{y\in S_n,\ x\le y\le z}\mathrm{sgn}(y)=0 .$$
items.strategy: By [[thm-r-polynomial-recursion-and-degree-bounds]](e), for $x<z$ the sum $\sum_y r_{x,y}\overline{r_{y,z}}$ is zero. Its bar symmetry (d) turns this into $\sum_y\mathrm{sgn}(y)r_{x,y}r_{y,z}=0$ after multiplying by $\mathrm{sgn}(z)$, and support (b) restricts to $y\in[x,z]$. Let $d=\ell(z)-\ell(x)$. The coefficient of $v^{-d}$ in each signed product is $\mathrm{sgn}(x)\mathrm{sgn}(z)\mathrm{sgn}(y)$: the two lowest R-coefficients contribute $\mathrm{sgn}(x)\mathrm{sgn}(z)$, and the outer factor contributes $\mathrm{sgn}(y)$. No other exponents contribute at degree $-d$. Thus the coefficient of $v^{-d}$ in the zero sum is $\mathrm{sgn}(x)\mathrm{sgn}(z)\sum_{x\le y\le z}\mathrm{sgn}(y)$, proving the assertion. The Bruhat interval is finite by [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]], and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis
items.statement: For each $w\in S_n$ there is a unique element $\underline H_w\in H_v(n)$ with (i) $\overline{\underline H_w}=\underline H_w$ and (ii) $\underline H_w\in H_w+\sum_{y<w}v\mathbb Z[v]\,H_y$ (the sum over the lower Bruhat ideal of $w$). The elements $\{\underline H_w\}_{w\in S_n}$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, and writing $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ one has $p_{w,w}=1$, $p_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, $p_{y,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for $y<w$, the bar-duality $p_{x,w}=\sum_{y}r_{x,y}\,\overline{p_{y,w}}$ (matrix form $P=R\bar P$), and the symmetry $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$. Moreover for $y<w$, with $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$: $p_{y,w}=v^{d}+\text{terms of strictly smaller degree}$ and $p_{y,w}\in v^{d}\,\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$; in particular every $\underline H_w$ has integer nonnegative coefficients in the standard basis with $p_{y,w}$ of fixed parity $d\bmod 2$.
items.strategy: Existence: for fixed $w$, set $p_{w,w}=1$ and induct down Bruhat order. For $x<w$, put $a_x=\sum_{x<y\le w}r_{x,y}\overline{p_{y,w}}$; the already constructed coefficient equations and both R-matrix inverse identities show $\overline{a_x}=-a_x$. If $a_x=\sum_n\gamma_nv^n$, set $p_{x,w}=\sum_{n>0}\gamma_nv^n$, the unique element of $v\mathbb Z[v]$ with $p_{x,w}-\overline{p_{x,w}}=a_x$. Comparing standard-basis coefficients proves bar invariance. A maximal-support argument proves uniqueness; the finite transition matrix is unitriangular, giving a basis. Coefficient comparison gives $P=R\bar P$. Induction using the top-degree and parity clauses of the R theorem shows $p_{x,w}=v^d+$ lower powers and $p_{x,w}\in v^d\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$: the $y=w$ term supplies the unique top degree, and all other terms have degree at most $d-2$. Apply the reversal helper and Bruhat inversion symmetry to obtain $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$. Only coefficientwise positivity invokes Elias–Williamson Corollary 1.2(1), under the exact owner authorization; identify the normalizations and triangular bases locally by uniqueness. All other clauses remain local; no Soergel–Hodge proof is asserted. No Choice is used.

items.title: Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials in the classical $q$-normalization
items.statement:
Identify $\mathbb Z[q]$ with $\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$ by $q\mapsto v^{-2}$. For $y\le w$ in $S_n$, put $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ and define the **Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial** $P_{y,w}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q]$ by $$P_{y,w}(v^{-2})=v^{-d}p_{y,w},$$ where $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ is the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]. The parity clause of that theorem makes the right side a polynomial in $v^{-2}$. items.title: Multiplication by a generator in the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis
items.statement: Let $s=s_i$ be a simple reflection and $w\in S_n$. In the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis $\{\underline H_w\}$ of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]: $$\underline H_s\,\underline H_w=\begin{cases}(v+v^{-1})\,\underline H_w,&sw<w,\\[2pt] \underline H_{sw}+\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{z\in S_n\\ sz<z<w}}\mu(z,w)\,\underline H_z,&sw>w,\end{cases}$$ and symmetrically $\underline H_w\underline H_s=(v+v^{-1})\underline H_w$ if $ws<w$, $\underline H_w\underline H_s=\underline H_{ws}+\sum_{zs<z<w}\mu(z,w)\underline H_z$ if $ws>w$. Here $\mu(z,w)$ is the coefficient of $v$ in $p_{z,w}$ ([[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]), which can be nonzero only when $\ell(w)-\ell(z)$ is odd; the sums are finite since $S_n$ is finite. In particular $\underline H_s\underline H_s=(v+v^{-1})\underline H_s$, and $\underline H_s\underline H_w=\underline H_{sw}$ when $sw>w$ and $\ell(w)\le1$. The span conclusion is for the ascent case $sw>w$: there, $\underline H_s\underline H_w$ lies in the span of $\underline H_{sw}$ and of the $\underline H_z$ with $z<w$ and $sz<z$.
items.strategy: Prove the left ascent case by comparing standard-basis coefficients in $\underline H_s\underline H_w$ with $\underline H_{sw}+\sum_{sz<z<w}\mu(z,w)\underline H_z$. The coefficient formula follows from the presented generator multiplication. When $sy<y$, the $z=y$ term cancels the constant term of $v^{-1}p_{y,w}$ because $\mu(y,w)$ is its coefficient of $v$; all other terms lie in $v\mathbb Z[v]$. When $sy>y$, induction on $\ell(w)$ gives $p_{y,z}=v p_{sy,z}$ for lower left descents and reduces the coefficient to $v f_{sy}+v p_{sy,sw}-p_{y,sw}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$; treat $y=w$ separately. The difference is bar-fixed and strictly lower, so uniqueness forces it to vanish. For $sw<w$, apply the ascent case to $sw$ and $(H_s-v^{-1})\underline H_s=0$, using induction on lower terms. Apply the reversal anti-automorphism to the left formulas for $w^{-1}$ to obtain the right formulas. The unresolved positivity clause of the basis supplier is not used; that supplier remains escalated. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial descent recursion
items.statement: Let $s=s_i$ be a simple reflection, $w\in S_n$ with $sw<w$, and $y\le w$. With $P_{x,z}:=0$ whenever $x\not\le z$, $$P_{y,w}(q)=q^{1-c}P_{sy,sw}(q)+q^{c}P_{y,sw}(q)-\!\!\!\sum_{\substack{y\le z\le sw\\ sz<z,\ \mu(z,sw)\ne0}}\!\!\!\mu(z,sw)\,q^{(\ell(w)-\ell(z))/2}P_{y,z}(q),$$ where $c=1$ if $sy<y$ and $c=0$ if $sy>y$; here $\mu$ is the coefficient defined in [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]] (so the summand only occurs for $\ell(sw)-\ell(z)$ odd, and $(\ell(w)-\ell(z))/2$ is then an integer). The same recursion holds with $s\in R(w)$ (right descents) after replacing each index $x$ by $x^{-1}$, using $P_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=P_{y,w}$ and $\mu(y^{-1},w^{-1})=\mu(y,w)$.
items.strategy: For the left descent sw<w, apply the KL-basis multiplication formula to the ascent product H̲_s H̲_{sw} and compare H_y coefficients after expanding in the standard basis. Derive the needed left standard-basis multiplication from reduced words and the quadratic relation. Convert the resulting p-coefficient equation using p_{x,z}=v^{ℓ(z)-ℓ(x)}P_{x,z}(v^{-2}); the μ parity clause makes each correction exponent integral. Obtain the right-descent formula by applying the left formula to inverse indices and using Bruhat inversion and inverse-index coefficient symmetry. All intervals and sums are finite; no Choice is used.

items.title: Inverse Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
items.statement:
For $x,w\in S_n$ set $$q'_{x,w}:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^m\sum_{x=z_0<z_1<\cdots<z_m=w}p_{z_0,z_1}p_{z_1,z_2}\cdots p_{z_{m-1},z_m}\in A,$$ where the inner sum is over strictly increasing Bruhat chains from $x$ to $w$, the $m=0$ chain occurs only when $x=w$, and $p_{u,v}$ are the coefficients of the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis ([[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]). Every chain lies in a finite Bruhat interval by [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]], so the sum is finite. If $x\not\le w$ there are no chains; if $x=w$, the empty chain gives $q'_{w,w}=1$. If $x<w$, each chain has at least one factor $p_{u,v}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ with $u<v$, so $q'_{x,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$.

Let $P=(p_{x,w})$ and $Q'=(q'_{x,w})$. The matrix $N:=P-I$ is strictly triangular on the finite Bruhat poset, hence nilpotent; the $(x,w)$ entry of $N^m$ is the sum of products over chains of $m$ strict steps. Therefore $$Q'=I-N+N^2-\cdots+(-1)^M N^M=(I+N)^{-1}=P^{-1},$$ where $M$ can be any integer at least the maximum strict-chain length. In particular, $Q'P=PQ'=I$ and $$\sum_zq'_{x,z}p_{z,w}=\delta_{x,w}=\sum_zp_{x,z}q'_{z,w}.$$

The **inverse Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials** in the classical sign convention are $q_{x,w}:=\mathrm{sgn}(x)\mathrm{sgn}(w)q'_{x,w}$. If $\Sigma$ is the diagonal matrix with entries $\Sigma_{x,x}=\mathrm{sgn}(x)$, then $Q=(q_{x,w})=\Sigma Q'\Sigma$. Equivalently, if $D_x$ is the basis of $H^*=\mathrm{Hom}_A(H,A)$ dual to the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis, then $$q'_{x,w}=D_x(H_w),$$ since $H_w=\sum_zq'_{z,w}\underline H_z$.
items.strategy: The chain sum is finite because each chain lies in the finite Bruhat interval [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]](e). Its diagonal term is the empty chain, equal to 1; for $x\not\le w$ no chain exists; and for $x<w$ every chain has at least one factor in $v\mathbb Z[v]$, so $q'_{x,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$. Let $N=P-I$. Since $P$ is unitriangular on the finite Bruhat poset, $N$ is nilpotent, and the chain sum is the entrywise finite sum $Q'=I-N+N^2-\cdots$, hence $Q'P=PQ'=I$. This also identifies $q'_{x,w}=D_x(H_w)$ for the functionals dual to the KL basis. The sign convention is $Q=sQ's$. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The Kazhdan–Lusztig inversion formula
items.statement: Let $P=(p_{x,w})$, $Q'=(q'_{x,w})$ and $R=(r_{x,y})$ be the triangular matrices of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]] and [[thm-r-polynomial-recursion-and-degree-bounds]]. Then (a) $P=R\bar P$, $\bar P=\bar RP$, and $R\bar R=\bar RR=1$; (b) $Q'P=PQ'=1$, and the inversion formulas $$\overline{q'_{x,w}}=\sum_{x\le z\le w}q'_{x,z}r_{z,w},\qquad \overline{q_{x,w}}=\sum_{x\le z\le w}q_{x,z}\overline{r_{z,w}}$$ hold, i.e. $\bar Q'=Q'R$ and $\bar Q=Q\bar R$; (c) for the dual basis $D_x(\underline H_w)=\delta_{x,w}$ from [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]], $D_x(H_w)=q'_{x,w}$. The inversion is proved from the bar-duality relations alone (no finite case check).
items.strategy: (a) $P=R\bar P$ is bar-duality from [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]; applying bar gives $\bar P=\bar RP$, and $R\bar R=\bar RR=1$ is from [[thm-r-polynomial-recursion-and-degree-bounds]]. (b) By [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]], $Q'=P^{-1}$. Inverting $P=R\bar P$ gives $Q'=\bar Q'\bar R$, hence $\bar Q'=Q'R$. With the sign matrix $S^2=1$, $Q=SQ'S$ and $\bar R=SRS$ give $\bar Q=Q\bar R$. (c) The coordinate functionals dual to the KL basis have standard-basis values given by $Q'$. All matrices are finite because $S_n$ is finite; no choice principle is used.

items.title: $L$-, $R$- and two-sided Kazhdan–Lusztig preorders and cells
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $C_w:=\underline H_w$ be the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis from [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], and let $S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_{n-1}\}$ be the simple reflections of $S_n$. For $x,y\in S_n$, write $x\leftarrow_L y$ if the coefficient of $C_x$ in $C_sC_y$ is nonzero for some $s\in S$, and write $x\leftarrow_R y$ if the coefficient of $C_x$ in $C_yC_s$ is nonzero for some $s\in S$. Define $x\le_L y$ if there is a finite chain $x=w_0,\ldots,w_m=y$ with $w_i\leftarrow_Lw_{i+1}$ for every $i<m$; define $\le_R$ using $\leftarrow_R$, and define $\le_{LR}$ by allowing either kind of step at each place. The length-zero chain makes each relation reflexive. Define $x\sim_Ly$ by $x\le_Ly$ and $y\le_Lx$, and similarly $\sim_R$ and $\sim_{LR}$. Their equivalence classes are the **left cells**, **right cells**, and **two-sided cells**.

For $w\in S_n$, set $L(w):=\{s\in S:sw<w\}$ and $R(w):=\{s\in S:ws<w\}$. The recorded properties are: $\le_L,\le_R,\le_{LR}$ are preorders; $x\le_Ly$ iff $x^{-1}\le_Ry^{-1}$; $x\le_Ly$ implies $R(y)\subseteq R(x)$ and $x\le_Ry$ implies $L(y)\subseteq L(x)$; consequently, elements of one left cell have equal right descent sets and elements of one right cell have equal left descent sets.

The multiplication formula [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-multiplication-formula]] gives the non-diagonal elementary left steps: if $sw>w$, then $C_{sw}$ occurs with coefficient $1$, and $C_z$ occurs with coefficient $\mu(z,w)$ exactly for the terms $z<w$, $sz<z$, and $\mu(z,w)\ne0$. If $sw<w$, the product is $(v+v^{-1})C_w$, so it gives only a diagonal step. (That diagonal coefficient is nonzero, but it adds no relation beyond the length-zero chain.)
items.strategy: Reflexivity comes from length-zero chains and transitivity from concatenation. The reversal anti-automorphism sends each Kazhdan–Lusztig basis vector to the vector indexed by its inverse, so it carries every elementary left coefficient to the corresponding right coefficient and yields inversion symmetry. For a left coefficient a_x of C_x in C_s C_y, t in R(y) gives (C_s C_y) C_t=(v+v^{-1})C_s C_y. If xt>x, the right multiplication formula makes the coefficient of C_x on the left zero: a leading term could reach x only from the descent index xt, and all lower corrections have t-descent indices. Thus a_x=0 since v+v^{-1} is nonzero in Z[v^{±1}]. The left-eigenvector argument gives the right-preorder descent inclusion. Mutual reachability gives equality of descent sets within cells. Finally, split the multiplication formula into its ascent and descent cases; in the descent case retain the nonzero diagonal coefficient while noting there are no non-diagonal steps. The proof is finite and uses no choice principle.

items.title: Knuth and dual Knuth equivalence for permutations
items.statement: Fix n≥1 and write S_n in the 1-based convention of def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n. Its zero-based realization in def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation is identified by the order-preserving shift on inputs and values. For a<b<c, allow the reversible contiguous-factor moves bca↔bac and cab↔acb. Knuth equivalence is the equivalence relation generated by finite chains of these moves (including length zero); dual Knuth equivalence is Knuth equivalence after inversion. The insertion tableau P(x) is obtained by row-inserting the one-line word of x from the empty tableau. Every elementary move preserves P, and two permutations are Knuth equivalent iff their insertion tableaux agree; this well-definedness/result is supplied by thm-knuth-equivalence-classes-are-insertion-tableau-fibers.
items.strategy: Definition item. The two reversible moves generate an equivalence relation: zero-length chains give reflexivity, reversing a chain gives symmetry, and concatenating chains gives transitivity. Inversion is a bijection, so it transports this equivalence relation to the dual one. The order-preserving shift between the two S_n conventions preserves all comparisons. The row-insertion definition supplies P; the assigned Knuth-fiber theorem establishes its invariance and the exact fiber characterization. No Choice is used.

items.title: Knuth classes are the fibers of the insertion tableau
items.statement: For permutations x,y∈S_n with RSK pairs (P(x),Q(x)) and (P(y),Q(y)), x∼_K y iff P(x)=P(y), and x∼_{dK}y iff Q(x)=Q(y). Thus the Knuth and dual Knuth classes are exactly the insertion- and recording-tableau fibers, and the induced maps from classes to standard tableaux of size n are bijections.
items.strategy: Direct row-bumping proof. Check the two Knuth relations on one increasing row: in each pair the final row agrees and the bumped words are either equal or another Knuth pair; induction down rows uses the proved standardness of each output. For the converse, read a tableau bottom-to-top, left-to-right: one insertion transforms the old row word to the new one by explicit Knuth moves along the bumping position. Induct on word length to connect every word to its tableau row word. RSK inversion symmetry gives the recording-tableau fiber statement, and the RSK bijection gives surjectivity of both class maps. No Choice is used.

items.title: Star operations on strings of adjacent simple reflections
items.statement: For n≥3 and r=s_i,t=s_{i+1}, let D_i={w∈S_n: exactly one of r,t is a right descent}. In each right coset of ⟨r,t⟩≅S_3, sort the entries in positions i,i+1,i+2 increasingly to obtain its unique shortest element w̃. The six elements are w̃, w̃r, w̃t, w̃rt, w̃tr, w̃rtr with lengths ℓ(w̃)+0,…,ℓ(w̃)+3; D_i consists of w̃r,w̃rt,w̃t,w̃tr. Define the right star involution by w̃r↔w̃rt and w̃t↔w̃tr. Define the left star on D_i⁻¹ by *w=((w⁻¹)^*)⁻¹. In one-line notation the two pairs are bac↔bca and acb↔cab, so w and w* differ by one Knuth move on positions i,i+1,i+2.
items.strategy: Definition item. The right coset permutes a consecutive three-position block. Its unique shortest representative sorts the three distinct entries: all inversions with positions outside the block have unchanged total contribution, while the internal inversion count is uniquely minimized at the sorted triple. The six S3 patterns have lengths 0,1,1,2,2,3 relative to this representative; exactly the four length-1 and length-2 patterns have one right descent. Pairing them as r↔rt and t↔tr defines an involution. The four one-line patterns are bac, bca, acb, cab and the paired moves are exactly the two Knuth relations. The left operation is conjugated by inversion.

items.title: Star operations are Knuth moves and preserve the relevant cells
items.statement: Let $D_i$ and $(-)^*$ be as in [[def-star-operations-on-the-symmetric-group]]. (a) For $w\in D_i$, $w^*$ is obtained from $w$ by one elementary Knuth relation on the letters in positions $i,i+1,i+2$; in particular $P(w^*)=P(w)$. Put $D_{ij}:=\{w\in D_i:ws_i<w,\ ws_{i+1}>w\}$ and $D_{ji}:=\{w\in D_i:ws_i>w,\ ws_{i+1}<w\}$. The restriction $K_{ij}$ of $(-)^*$ is a bijection $D_{ij}\to D_{ji}$ whose inverse is $K_{ji}$. (b) For every $w\in D_i$, if $a$ and $b$ are the shorter and longer, respectively, of $\{w,w^*\}$, then $\mu(a,b)=1$ and $w^*\sim_Rw$; by inversion, $^*w\sim_Lw$ whenever $w^{-1}\in D_i$. (c) Inside the rank-two subgroup $W_I=\langle s_i,s_{i+1}\rangle\cong S_3$, every Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial $P_{x,y}$ with $x\le y$ is $1$, and $\mu(x,y)=1$ exactly for Bruhat covers $x\lessdot y$. For every shortest representative $\widetilde w$ of a right $W_I$-coset, the ambient pairs $\widetilde w s_i\lessdot\widetilde w s_i s_{i+1}$ and $\widetilde w s_{i+1}\lessdot\widetilde w s_{i+1}s_i$ therefore also have $\mu$-coefficient $1$.
items.strategy: Part (a) follows from the one-line star table and the Knuth-fiber theorem. For the rank-two calculation, compute the six A2 basis elements inside the subgroup from the multiplication formula and standard quadratic relation; this gives P=1 and cover mu-coefficients. In the ambient group, each pair related by the star table is a Bruhat cover, so the basis theorem gives p=v and hence mu=1. For each pair, the ascent multiplication formula gives one right coefficient edge with coefficient 1; the opposite edge is the mu-term in multiplication by the other generator, since the upper star element ascends and the lower one descends. Thus the pair is right-cell equivalent. Inversion gives the left-star statement. The full global KL basis of an arbitrary shifted coset is not asserted to be supported in that coset.

items.statement:
Fix $i$, let $D_{ij},D_{ji},K_{ij}$ be as in [[lem-dual-knuth-star-operations-give-antiparallel-kazhdan-lusztig-graph-edges]], and use the convention $\mu(u|v)
e0$ of [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]. (a) **Edge transport.** For $y,w\in D_{ij}$ with $y
e w$ and $\mu(y|w)
e0$ one has $\mu(K_{ij}(y)|K_{ij}(w))
e0$, and in fact the transported leading coefficients agree: $\mu(K_{ij}(y)|K_{ij}(w))=\mu(y|w)$, the transported pair being taken in the Bruhat order in which it is comparable. (b) **Transport of the preorder.** For $x,y\in D_{ij}$: $x\le_Ly\iff K_{ij}(x)\le_LK_{ij}(y)$ and $x\le_Ry\iff K_{ij}(x)\le_RK_{ij}(y)$; in particular $x\sim_Ly\iff K_{ij}(x)\sim_LK_{ij}(y)$ and $x\sim_Ry\iff K_{ij}(x)\sim_RK_{ij}(y)$.
items.strategy: (a) Put $\pi_{a,b}=p_{a,b}/v$. Derive the right-descent recursion from [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomial-recursion]] and mixed-descent vanishing from [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-multiplication-formula]]. Handle the same-coset covers directly; for distinct cosets compare constant terms in the two recursion cases, with the complete symmetric orientation recorded in Casselman, Theorem 6.2, §§4.4–4.5 and §5.3. (b) Right-preorder transport follows from the elementwise right-cell equivalence in [[lem-dual-knuth-star-operations-give-antiparallel-kazhdan-lusztig-graph-edges]](b). For left-preorder transport, let $I_s,I_t$ be the spans of KL basis elements with the respective right descents and $J=I_s\cap I_t$. Right multiplication by the adjacent KL generator induces inverse left-module maps $I_s/J\leftrightarrow I_t/J$ and sends each quotient basis element to its star. The mixed-descent coefficient identity proves the basis action locally. Right-descent monotonicity traps every intermediate element of a left-preorder chain in the one-sided domain. No p-canonical basis or Choice is used.

items.title: Equal insertion or recording tableaux imply right or left equivalence
items.statement: For $x,y\in S_n$: (a) $P(x)=P(y)\Rightarrow x\sim_Ry$; (b) $Q(x)=Q(y)\Rightarrow x\sim_Ly$. Equivalently: a Knuth class lies in a single right cell and a dual Knuth class lies in a single left cell.
items.strategy: (b) By the symmetry theorem $P(w^{-1})=Q(w)$ ([[cor-rsk-symmetry-under-inversion]]), $Q(x)=Q(y)$ gives $P(x^{-1})=P(y^{-1})$, so $x^{-1},y^{-1}$ are Knuth equivalent ([[thm-knuth-equivalence-classes-are-insertion-tableau-fibers]]); a chain of elementary Knuth moves joins them, each move is a right star step on the corresponding domain ([[def-star-operations-on-the-symmetric-group]]), and each such step stays in a right cell ([[lem-dual-knuth-star-operations-give-antiparallel-kazhdan-lusztig-graph-edges]](b)); hence $x^{-1}\sim_Ry^{-1}$, and inversion gives $x\sim_Ly$ ([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-kazhdan-lusztig-preorders-and-cells]]). (a) is the same argument applied to $x^{-1},y^{-1}$ and the dual-Knuth half of [[thm-knuth-equivalence-classes-are-insertion-tableau-fibers]], or directly by inversion. This is [Ariki, Proposition 3.8]. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Left equivalence forces equality of recording tableaux in type A
items.statement: For $x,y\in S_n$: $x\sim_Ly\Rightarrow Q(x)=Q(y)$.
items.strategy: Prove locally that adjacent descents of the word are exactly the descent positions of its recording tableau, and that among standard tableaux of the fixed shape lambda, the column-superstandard tableau is determined by its descent set, using containment in that final shape to exclude additions below already complete columns. Replace each endpoint by the unique permutation with its column-superstandard insertion tableau and the same recording tableau, using [[prop-same-insertion-or-recording-tableaux-imply-cell-equivalence]]. Join each replacement to the diagonal RSK permutation by a Knuth path; carry both paths across the other endpoint using the rank-two star operation and [[lem-kazhdan-lusztig-mu-edges-and-left-cells-are-transported-by-star-operations]](b). Compare the resulting column-block lengths from their equal right descent sets, then explicitly obtain shape(Q(w_prime))=lambda from the locally compared insertion shapes and RSK common shape, and use the fixed-shape descent correspondence and RSK uniqueness to identify the recording tableaux. Ariki, §3.4, is the source route; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Kazhdan–Lusztig cells of type A are classified by RSK tableaux
items.statement: For $x,y\in S_n$, with the RSK tableaux $P,Q$ of [[thm-robinson-schensted-correspondence]] (insertion tableau and recording tableau of the one-line word): $$x\sim_Ly\iff Q(x)=Q(y),\qquad x\sim_Ry\iff P(x)=P(y),\qquad x\sim_{LR}y\iff \operatorname{sh}(Q(x))=\operatorname{sh}(Q(y)).$$ Here $\sim_L,\sim_R,\sim_{LR}$ are the cell equivalence relations of [[def-left-right-and-two-sided-kazhdan-lusztig-preorders-and-cells]]; the chosen convention is displayed: **left cells are the fibers of the recording tableau**, **right cells are the fibers of the insertion tableau**, and **two-sided cells are the fibers of the shape map** (note $\operatorname{sh}(P(w))=\operatorname{sh}(Q(w))$). Consequently the left cells of $S_n$ are in bijection with the standard tableaux of size $n$, the right cells likewise, and the two-sided cells with the partitions of $n$.
items.strategy: Left classification uses the local recording-tableau implication and converse. Right classification follows by inversion and RSK symmetry. For two-sided equivalence implies equal shape, invoke only Geck Corollary5.6(c)'s authorized forward implication, after locally checking u=v^-1, relations/bar, triangular-basis uniqueness and nonzero simple-product coefficient/preorder-chain correspondence. Equal shape implies two-sided equivalence by the unique RSK preimage of (P(x),Q(y)). Counts use local RSK surjectivity and canonical standard tableaux. No stronger tableau-dominance premise or local Murphy/leading-matrix proof is claimed. No Choice is used.

title: Kazhdan–Lusztig Bases, Polynomials, and Cells — Examples

items.title: The Kazhdan–Lusztig bases of $S_2$ and $S_3$
items.statement: Work in the normalization of [[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]], write permutations in one-line notation, and put $q=v^{-2}$ as in [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]. (a) In $S_2$: $r_{\mathrm{id},21}=v-v^{-1}$, $\underline H_{\mathrm{id}}=H_{\mathrm{id}}$, $\underline H_{21}=H_{21}+vH_{\mathrm{id}}$, $P_{\mathrm{id},21}(q)=1$, $\mu(\mathrm{id},21)=1$ and $\underline H_{21}^2=(v+v^{-1})\underline H_{21}$. (b) In $S_3$ the bar images of the standard basis are $$\overline{H_{132}}=H_{132}+(v-v^{-1})H_{123},\qquad \overline{H_{213}}=H_{213}+(v-v^{-1})H_{123},$$ $$\overline{H_{231}}=H_{231}+(v-v^{-1})(H_{132}+H_{213})+(v^2-2+v^{-2})H_{123},$$ $$\overline{H_{312}}=H_{312}+(v-v^{-1})(H_{132}+H_{213})+(v^2-2+v^{-2})H_{123},$$ $$\overline{H_{321}}=H_{321}+(v-v^{-1})(H_{231}+H_{312})+(v^2-2+v^{-2})(H_{132}+H_{213})+(v^3-2v+2v^{-1}-v^{-3})H_{123},$$ the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis is $$\underline H_{123}=H_{123},\quad \underline H_{132}=H_{132}+vH_{123},\quad \underline H_{213}=H_{213}+vH_{123},$$ $$\underline H_{231}=H_{231}+v(H_{132}+H_{213})+v^2H_{123},\quad \underline H_{312}=H_{312}+v(H_{132}+H_{213})+v^2H_{123},$$ $$\underline H_{321}=H_{321}+v(H_{231}+H_{312})+v^2(H_{132}+H_{213})+v^3H_{123},$$ all $P_{y,w}(q)$ with $y\le w$ equal $1$, and $\mu(y,w)=1$ exactly when $y\lessdot w$ is a cover of the Bruhat order on $S_3$ (the eight covers $(123,132)$, $(123,213)$, $(132,231)$, $(132,312)$, $(213,231)$, $(213,312)$, $(231,321)$, $(312,321)$ in one-line notation). (c) Multiplication checks: $\underline H_{21}^2=(v+v^{-1})\underline H_{21}$ and, in the case $sw>w$ with one $\mu$-edge, $\underline H_{132}\underline H_{231}=\underline H_{321}+\underline H_{132}$ (here $s_2\cdot 231=321$ and $s_2\cdot 132=123<132$, so the sum in [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-multiplication-formula]] has the single term $\mu(132,231)=1$).
items.strategy: For S2, compute the rank-one bar coefficient and identify the triangular bar-fixed basis element, then calculate its square and read P and mu. For S3, expand the bar images multiplicatively from the two simple generators, construct the six candidates as 1, A, B, AB, BA, BAB−B, and apply uniqueness of the triangular bar-fixed basis. Read the polynomial coefficients and mu values from these expansions, list the covers by reduced subwords, and apply the generator multiplication formulas to the stated ascent and descent cases. The calculations are finite and choice-free.

items.title: The $R$- and Kazhdan–Lusztig recursions on a small singular interval
items.statement: In $S_4$, written in one-line notation, let $b:=s_2=1324$ and $w:=s_2s_1s_3s_2=3412$ (a reduced word of length $4$; the two middle generators commute). (a) The interval $[b,w]$ has exactly ten elements: $1324$; $1342,1423,2314,3124$; $1432,2413,3142,3214$; and $3412$. (b) For comparable pairs in this interval the only Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial different from $1$ is $P_{b,w}(q)=1+q$; so $\mu(b,w)=1$, and $(b,w)$ is a $\mu$-pair with $\ell(w)-\ell(b)=3>1$: $\mu$-pairs need not be covers. All other $\mu$-pairs inside the interval are covers, and all $r_{y,z}$ for $y,z\in[b,w]$ are the corresponding Laurent polynomials read off from [[thm-r-polynomial-recursion-and-degree-bounds]]. (c) The descent recursion of [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomial-recursion]] at $y=b$, $w$ and $s=s_2$ (a left descent of $w$, with $sw=2413$ and $sb=1234=\mathrm{id}$, so $c=1$) reads $$P_{b,w}(q)=P_{\mathrm{id},2413}(q)+qP_{b,2413}(q)-\!\!\!\sum_{\substack{b\le z\le 2413\\ s_2z<z,\ \mu(z,2413)\ne0}}\!\!\!\mu(z,2413)\,q^{(4-\ell(z))/2}P_{b,z}(q);$$ the sum is empty because $[b,2413]=\{1324,1423,2314,2413\}$ and its only element with $s_2z<z$ is $1324$, for which $\mu(1324,2413)=0$; since $P_{\mathrm{id},2413}=P_{b,2413}=1$, the recursion returns $P_{b,w}=1+q$, in agreement with (b). (d) The inverse Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial of [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]] is $q'_{b,w}=-v-v^3$, while $q'_{b,1342}=q'_{b,1423}=q'_{b,2314}=q'_{b,3124}=-v$ and $q'_{b,1432}=q'_{b,2413}=q'_{b,3142}=q'_{b,3214}=v^2$; the matrix identity $\sum_zq'_{x,z}p_{z,w}=\delta_{x,w}$ of [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-inversion-formula]] holds on the ten-point interval. In particular the inverse coefficients are not all nonnegative even though all $p_{y,z}$ are.
items.strategy: Enumerate the reduced subwords of $s_2s_1s_3s_2$ and retain those above $b=s_2$; record every comparable pair. The degree bound and constant term give $P=1$ at gaps at most two. For $2413=s_1s_3s_2$, the product of the three simple KL elements is bar-fixed and triangular, giving $P_{\mathrm{id},2413}=1$. Apply the left descent recursion with $s=s_2$ on the actual interval $[b,2413]=\{1324,1423,2314,2413\}$; the sole descent candidate $b$ has even length gap and hence zero mu. This gives $P_{b,w}=1+q$. Compute all R-coefficients as $(v-v^{-1})^{\ell(z)-\ell(y)}$ on comparable pairs in this interval, using the R-recursion. Invert the resulting triangular p-matrix: each gap-two interval has two middle elements, and the bottom-to-top calculation gives $q\prime_{b,w}=-v-v^3$. No choice principle is used.

items.title: RSK cells in $S_3$ and $S_4$
items.statement: Use the RSK correspondence of [[thm-robinson-schensted-correspondence]] for the one-line word (insertion tableau $P$, recording tableau $Q$; the row insertion is [[def-row-insertion-and-bumping-route]]), and write a standard tableau as its rows separated by bars. (a) In $S_3$: $123\mapsto(123,123)$, $132\mapsto(12|3,12|3)$, $213\mapsto(13|2,13|2)$, $231\mapsto(13|2,12|3)$, $312\mapsto(12|3,13|2)$, $321\mapsto(1|2|3,1|2|3)$ (pairs $(P,Q)$). (b) The left cells of $S_3$ are the four $Q$-fibers $\{123\}$, $\{132,231\}$, $\{213,312\}$, $\{321\}$; the right cells are the four $P$-fibers $\{123\}$, $\{132,312\}$, $\{213,231\}$, $\{321\}$; the two-sided cells are the three shape fibers $\{123\}$, $\{132,213,231,312\}$, $\{321\}$. (c) In $S_4$ the ten left cells are the ten $Q$-fibers: $[1234]:\{1234\}$; $[12|34]:\{2413,3412\}$; $[123|4]:\{1243,1342,2341\}$; $[124|3]:\{1324,1423,2314\}$; $[13|24]:\{2143,3142\}$; $[134|2]:\{2134,3124,4123\}$; $[12|3|4]:\{1432,2431,3421\}$; $[13|2|4]:\{3241,4132,4231\}$; $[14|2|3]:\{3214,4213,4312\}$; $[1|2|3|4]:\{4321\}$; these are in bijection with the ten standard tableaux of size $4$. (d) Right descent sets are constant on left cells but do not determine them: in $S_4$ the permutations $1324$ and $2413$ both have right descent set $\{s_2\}$, while $Q(1324)=[124|3]$ and $Q(2413)=[12|34]$, so $1324$ and $2413$ lie in different left cells.
items.strategy: (a) Direct row insertion, terminating in the listed tableaux; (b),(c) apply the classification theorem [[thm-type-a-kazhdan-lusztig-cells-are-classified-by-rsk-tableaux]] to the resulting $P,Q$ pairs. For (d), compute the inversion lengths: $1324$ has length $1$ and $1324s_2=1234$ has length $0$, while $2413$ has length $3$ and $2413s_2=2143$ has length $2$; multiplication by $s_1,s_3$ increases length in both cases. The recording tableaux from (c) differ, so the theorem puts the two permutations in different left cells. No choice principle is used.
